sources.title: CBD leads Jakarta apartment price gains but growth remains uneven
41,609 Property for Sale near MRT Station, Jakarta - FazWaz.id

questions.question: Under the land rules described in the source, which type of title can a foreigner NOT hold in Indonesia?
questions.explanation: The source states plainly that freehold land, Hak Milik, is closed to foreigners; they instead buy a long lease, a Hak Pakai title or an apartment unit. Hak Pakai and leases are the routes the source describes as available in practice.
questions.evidence: A foreigner cannot hold freehold land (Hak Milik).

questions.question: A foreign buyer wants a Hak Pakai house in Jakarta. Besides paying the price, what does the source say this requires?

options.A: A residence permit and meeting the state's minimum price
options.B: Only written approval from the local neighbourhood association
options.C: Converting the title to Hak Milik within five years of purchase
options.D: An Indonesian spouse named as co-owner on the certificate

questions.explanation: Hak Pakai houses are a registered asset, but the source notes they require a residence permit and a minimum price. A lease, by contrast, is open to anyone but is only a contract.
questions.evidence: they require a residence permit and a minimum price

questions.question: How does the source contrast a lease with a Hak Pakai title for a foreign buyer?

options.A: A lease grants the same rights as freehold for its full term
options.B: A lease requires a residence permit, while Hak Pakai does not
options.C: A lease is cheaper and open to anyone, but it is a contract rather than a title
options.D: A lease is a registered title that can be mortgaged to a bank

questions.explanation: The source frames the trade-off clearly: leases are cheaper and unrestricted but give contractual rights, not a registered title. That is why it urges buyers to read what the certificate actually says before comparing prices.
questions.evidence: A lease is cheaper and available to anyone, but it is a contract, not a title.

questions.question: For a foreign buyer working with a budget of roughly $70,000–350,000, what does the source say about Jakarta specifically?

options.A: Jakarta is the only Indonesian market where foreigners may buy below $100,000
options.B: Jakarta fixes every foreign purchase at exactly $170,000 per unit
options.C: The minimum purchase price for foreigners can shut Jakarta out below about $170,000
options.D: Jakarta imposes no minimum price on foreigners, unlike Bali

questions.explanation: The source uses the foreigner minimum price as the reason a mid-sized budget may not stretch to Jakarta at all, with roughly $170,000 as the threshold. The minimum price is a state rule, not a per-unit price cap or a Bali-only restriction.
questions.evidence: why a foreigner's minimum purchase price can shut Jakarta out below about $170,000

questions.question: According to the Bank Indonesia data cited in the source, how much did Greater Jakarta residential prices rise year-on-year in Q1 2025?
questions.explanation: Q1 2025 growth was 1.07%. The 1.39% figure belongs to Q4 2024 and 1.96% to Q3 2023, while 0.47% refers to a real-terms decline.

questions.question: What does the run of Bank Indonesia growth figures from Q3 2023 through Q1 2025 indicate about Greater Jakarta's residential market?

options.A: Nominal prices have been falling sharply quarter after quarter
options.B: Growth has accelerated in each successive quarter
options.C: Price growth has been moderate but steadily decelerating
options.D: Prices have been completely flat, recording zero growth

questions.explanation: Growth slipped from 1.96% to 1.39% to 1.07%, which the source summarises as moderate and decelerating. Prices were still rising in nominal terms, so a sharp fall is the wrong reading.
questions.evidence: Jakarta's residential property market has shown moderate and decelerating price growth over the 2023–2025 period.

questions.question: On top of the agreed sale price, how much should a Jakarta buyer budget for acquisition costs such as BPHTB, notary and legal fees, and VAT?
questions.explanation: The source benchmarks total buyer-side acquisition costs at 6.5% to 9% of value. The 9.5% to 14% range is the separate round-trip cost of buying and reselling.
questions.evidence: typically represent 6.5% to 9% of the property value

questions.question: What is the estimated round-trip cost of buying a Jakarta property and then reselling it?
questions.explanation: The source puts the full buy-then-sell cost at roughly 9.5% to 14%. The narrower 6.5% to 9% band covers only buyer-side acquisition costs.
questions.evidence: round-trip cost of buying and then reselling is estimated at roughly 9.5% to 14%

questions.question: What was Jakarta's citywide average residential price as of mid-2025?

options.A: Approximately IDR 5 million per square meter
options.B: Approximately IDR 12 million per square meter
options.C: Approximately IDR 50 million per square meter
options.D: Approximately IDR 25 million per square meter

questions.explanation: The source cites a citywide average of about IDR 25 million per square meter in mid-2025. It also stresses that this average masks wide variation between locations and buildings.
questions.evidence: The citywide average residential price stood at approximately IDR 25 million per square meter as of mid-2025

questions.question: According to Colliers, what is primarily driving Jakarta apartment price growth?
questions.explanation: Colliers attributes growth mainly to end users, noting that investors are directing capital to more liquid asset classes, which limits speculative pressure on residential values.
questions.source_title: CBD leads Jakarta apartment price gains but growth remains uneven
questions.evidence: price growth is being driven primarily by end-user demand
